[[Nigerian chieftaincy|Chief]] '''James Nwoye Adichie''' {{Audio|Ig-James Nwoye Adichie.ogg|Listen}} (1 March 1932 – 10 June 2020)<ref name="auto" /> was a Nigerian academic who served as a first professor of [[statistics]] at the [[University of Nigeria]] [[Nsukka]]. He was the father of writer [[Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie]].

== Life ==
Adichie was born on 1 March 1932 in Abba, located in [[Njikoka]], [[Anambra State]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite news | title=James Nwoye Adichie (1932 – 2020) |newspaper=[[The Sun (Nigeria)|The Sun]]| date=3 July 2020 | url=https://thesun.ng/james-nwoye-adichie-1932-2020/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria| access-date=7 March 2025}}</ref> Soon after his birth, he relocated to [[Awkuzu]] and later to [[Nimo, Nigeria|Nimo]], where he attended Nimo Primary School for his early education.<ref>{{Cite news | last=Eleweke | first=Titus | title=Reminiscences with Prof James Nwoye Adichie |newspaper=[[Daily Trust]]| date=20 October 2019 | url=https://dailytrust.com/reminiscences-with-prof-james-nwoye-adichie/ | access-date=7 March 2025 | archive-date=12 March 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312094909/https://dailytrust.com/reminiscences-with-prof-james-nwoye-adichie/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

In 1957, he enrolled in the [[University College, Ibadan]], to study mathematics, graduating in 1960. He then joined the research department at the [[Central Bank of Nigeria]] (CBN).<ref name="auto"/> After leaving the CBN, Adichie returned to academia as a mathematics instructor at the [[Nigerian College of Arts, Science and Technology]] in [[Enugu State]] and later became an assistant lecturer at the [[University of Nigeria, Nsukka]]. In September 1963, he departed Nigeria to pursue a PhD in statistics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he studied under [[Erich Leo Lehmann]]. He earned his doctorate in 1966, becoming the first Nigerian to receive a PhD in statistics from UC Berkeley.<ref>{{cite web | title=James Nwoye Adichie | website=Department of Statistics | publisher=University of California, Berkeley | url=https://statistics.berkeley.edu/people/james-nwoye-adichie | access-date=7 March 2025 | archive-date=12 March 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312120259/https://statistics.berkeley.edu/people/james-nwoye-adichie | url-status=live }}</ref> In 1976, he became the inaugural professor of statistics at the [[University of Nigeria]] and later served as its [[Deputy Vice Chancellor]] from 1980 to 1984, retiring in 1997.<ref name="auto"/>

Throughout his career, Adichie published articles in academic journals and magazines.<ref name="auto"/> His academic work included a fellowship at the [[University of Sheffield]] in England and a term as a visiting professor at [[San Diego State University]] in California, as well as serving as the first editor of the ''[[Journal of Statistical Association of Nigeria]]''.<ref name="auto"/> On 2 May 2015, while returning to Abba from [[Nsukka]], Adichie was kidnapped.<ref>{{Cite news | last=Akinkugbe | first=Oladipo | title=My father was targeted because of me, says Chimamanda |newspaper=[[TheCable]]| date=31 May 2015 | url=https://www.thecable.ng/father-targeted-says-chimamanda/ | access-date=7 March 2025 | archive-date=12 March 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312091733/https://www.thecable.ng/father-targeted-says-chimamanda/ | url-status=live }}</ref> According to reports from [[Pulse Nigeria]], his daughter, [[Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie]], explained in ''[[The New York Times]]'' that her presence was a factor in the abduction.<ref name="NYT">{{cite web | last=Adichie | first=Chimamanda Ngozi | title=Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie: My Father's Kidnapping | website=The New York Times | date=30 May 2015 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/05/31/opinion/sunday/chimamanda-ngozi-adichie-my-fathers-kidnapping.html?smid=tw-nytopinion&_r=1 | access-date=7 March 2025}}</ref> He was released three days later after payment of a ransom.<ref name="NYT"/><ref name="pulse.ng">{{Cite news | title=Nigerian author speaks on father's kidnapping |newspaper=[[Pulse Nigeria]]| date=12 January 2016 | url=https://www.pulse.ng/articles/ece-frontpage/chimamanda-adichie-nigerian-author-speaks-on-fathers-kidnapping-2024080611051936190 | access-date=7 March 2025 | archive-date=12 March 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312105550/https://www.pulse.ng/articles/ece-frontpage/chimamanda-adichie-nigerian-author-speaks-on-fathers-kidnapping-2024080611051936190 | url-status=live }}</ref>

==Legacy==
Adichie was the "Odelora Abba", a [[Nigerian Chieftaincy|Nigerian chieftaincy title]]. A member of the Nigerian National Advisory Council on Statistics, he was one of the figures who reorganised the Federal Office of Statistics that was later reformed to the [[National Bureau of Statistics, Nigeria|National Bureau of Statistics]].<ref name="auto"/>
